issues.failure_explanation: The coefficient of the strictly increasing polynomial P on every interval I^j is h-delta^mu. The lemma imposes no condition making it positive: if h<delta^mu, phi decreases there. Even the later hypothesis h>=delta^mu permits equality, in which case phi and every psi_q are constant throughout each I_q^j, so they are not strictly increasing and their derivatives vanish on entire intervals.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require h>delta^mu wherever strict monotonicity is asserted, and perturb numerical parameter choices that currently set h=delta^mu.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed strict monotonicity and the assertion that derivatives vanish only at interval endpoints fail in allowed parameter cases, including the equality case used in the numerical setup.
issues.title: Monotonicity fails when the polynomial-piece increment is nonpositive
issues.why_classification: A strict local parameter inequality restores the construction without changing its approximation rate or architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We also introduce a new parameter $J=\lceil\frac 1 {N\delta}\rceil=\lceil\frac 1 h \rceil,$

where we verify from \eqref{shapfunc0} directly that
$$\phi(1-(q-1)\delta)=1+\phi(-(q-1)\delta)=1+\phi((1-q)\delta).$$

issues.failure_explanation: The identity phi(t+1)=phi(t)+1 follows from the block construction only when 1 is an integer multiple of h, namely Jh=1. With J=ceil(1/h), this need not hold. Thus the denominator in the definition of psi_q cannot generally be replaced by 1, and the conclusions psi_q(1)=1, range [0,1], and h=1/J used later are unsupported.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Impose 1/h=J as an integer throughout, as the algorithm already does, or retain the actual normalization denominator and redo all formulas and estimates that use unit-periodic increments.
issues.overall_effect: For generic allowed delta, the inner-function formulas, their ranges, mapped-center formulas, and the stated conversion of the error bound from h^alpha to J^{-alpha} are unreliable.
issues.title: Normalization and endpoint formulas assume Jh=1 although J is defined by a ceiling
issues.why_classification: The integer-reciprocal restriction is a local condition compatible with the advertised asymptotic parameter choices and preserves the rate.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For each $q,$ letting $y_{j_p}=\phi_q(c_q^{j_p}),$ we note that    $c_q^{j_p}\in I_q^{j_p}$ are mapped by the polynomial piece $P$, so $y_{j_p}$  all rational numbers (see \eqref{shapfunc0}). Thus, $a_q^{\bs j}$ are distinct for fixed $q$.
a_q^{\bs j}=h\sum_{p\in {\mathcal J}_{\rm in}} \lambda_p j_p +\Big(\frac  {h+\delta^\mu} 2-\phi((1-q)\delta) \Big)\sum_{p\in {\mathcal J}_{\rm in}} \lambda_p+ \sum_{r\in {\mathcal J}_{1}} \lambda_r,

issues.failure_explanation: The mapped center values are not necessarily rational: they contain h, delta^mu, and phi((1-q)delta), for which no rationality assumptions are imposed. Rational independence of the lambda_p only excludes rational-coefficient relations. Indeed, for d=2 and q=1, write C=(h+delta^mu)/2. The center images for index pairs (0,-1) and (-1,1) are lambda_1 C and lambda_2(C+h). Choosing the allowed irrational ratio lambda_1/lambda_2=(C+h)/C produces equality while keeping lambda_1 and lambda_2 rationally independent. The cited generic nowhere-dense statement also cannot establish that the specifically constructed values avoid its exceptional set.

failure_location.quote:
Let $\bs \lambda=(\lambda_1, \ldots, \lambda_d)$  be a sequence of rationally independent numbers.
 Then the images   $a_q^{\bs j}$ of the Kolmogorov maps of $ \bs c_q^{\bs j}$ in \eqref{aqJaj} are all distinct.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Withdraw the general rational-independence alternative and retain a separately proved collision-free special choice, or add and prove a genuinely sufficient noncollision condition for the constructed center values.
issues.overall_effect: The rationally-independent branch of the encoded-data and outer-function construction may contain collisions with incompatible sampled values, so the corresponding branch of the main theorem is unsupported.
issues.title: Rational independence does not ensure distinct mapped centers
issues.why_classification: A complete repair requires a new separation argument or a meaningful restriction of the admitted lambda regime, but the special Sprecher-like branch could remain.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: a set of  numbers $\{\lambda_p\}_{p=1}^d$ are called {\em rationally independent},  {\em  if an equation $\sum_{p=1}^d r_p \lambda_p= 0$ with rational $r_p$ is possible only if all $r_p=0$}

issues.failure_explanation: Distinct arbitrary real exponents do not imply rational independence of their exponentials. For example, theta_1=0 and theta_2=ln 2 are distinct members of [0,1], but their exponentials are 1 and 2 and satisfy 2e^{theta_1}-e^{theta_2}=0. Normalizing them preserves this dependence.

failure_location.quote:
according to Lindeman's theorem 
{\rm(}see \cite[P.\! 71]{Shidlovskii1989}{\rm)}, one can choose $\hat \lambda_p=e^{\theta_p},$ where $ \theta_p$ are distinct numbers in $[0,1]$, and then set $\lambda_p=\hat \lambda_p /\sum_{j=1}^d \hat \lambda_j$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the exponents to a class for which the invoked transcendence theorem actually supplies linear independence, or remove this example.
issues.overall_effect: The stated practical recipe can supply weights that violate the hypothesis it is claimed to ensure.
issues.title: The proposed exponential weights need not be rationally independent
issues.why_classification: Only the example of admissible weights is affected; valid rationally independent weights can be selected by another standard construction.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then, for any  fixed level  $ 1\le q\le N,$  we extract  the data for interpolation at each row
if $\bs i$ is not unique, it is free to choose any index

issues.failure_explanation: The procedure defines many row-specific functions g_q^{j_p} and chooses among them using the full point x and a nearest-center index, not solely using t=Psi_q(x). Consequently it does not define a single-valued univariate function g_q(t), and two points with the same Psi_q value can be assigned different rows and outputs. The neighbor-selection equation is itself not an argmin: it equates an image value to a distance, leaves l undefined, can reference out-of-range indices, and its claimed uniqueness is false—for an interior center, the two opposite neighbors in one coordinate have equal mapped distance. Moreover, no condition ensures Psi_q(x) lies in the selected interpolation interval, so the proof cannot use S(z) in [0,1].
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must construct a globally single-valued univariate C^2 function g_q on the entire image of Psi_q and prove that every evaluation uses local sample values close enough to x to support the Hölder estimate.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised outer functions, the superposition f_N=sum_q g_q composed with Psi_q, its C^2 smoothness, and the main approximation guarantee are not well defined or proved.
issues.title: The row-dependent construction does not define univariate outer functions
issues.why_classification: Repairing the defect requires a new global outer-function construction and compatibility argument, which is central proof architecture rather than a local correction.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: To deal with such partial hypercubes, we  shift their centers to $x_p=0,1.$  More precisely, we re-set $c_q^{-1}=0$ and  $c_q^{J-1}=1$

issues.failure_explanation: After a partial interval's center is relocated to a boundary endpoint, its maximum distance is not half its length. For example, at q=N the left partial interval I_N^{-1} intersected with [0,1] is [0,(N-1)delta], while its relocated center is 0; its far endpoint is therefore (N-1)delta away, twice the asserted one-dimensional bound. The analogous nearest-center bound for gap cases is likewise not established with the factor 1/2.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redo the boundary and gap geometry using bounds of order sqrt(d)h rather than sqrt(d)h/2 and propagate the resulting larger constant through the proof.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit constant in the main uniform error estimate is not proved, independently of the outer-function defect.
issues.title: Boundary partial cubes violate the center-distance estimates
issues.why_classification: A routine local enlargement of the constant preserves the O(h^alpha) rate and all parameter regimes.
